content:
# 1 Enoch Chapter 104 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 104:2 — 'shine as the lights of heaven'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "ye-shall-shine-as-the-lights-of-heaven" | Literal; cf. Daniel 12:3 |
| LOGOS | "you shall shine as the lights of heaven" | Formal; preserves the simile |
| PNEUMA | "You will shine like stars in the sky" | 'Stars in the sky' for 'lights of heaven' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'lights of heaven.' The phrase mäse'ata samay (lights of the sky/heaven) is the term used — 'lights of heaven' is more literal and theologically resonant than PNEUMA's 'stars in the sky.' The connection to Daniel 12:3 ("those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament") is preserved by the formal rendering.

---

## 104:3 — 'cry for judgment' — rhetorical imperative

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "in-your-cry, cry-for-judgment" | Literal; reduplication |
| LOGOS | "in your cry, cry for judgment" | Formal; preserves the reduplication |
| PNEUMA | "Keep crying out for justice" | 'Justice' for 'judgment'; drops the reduplication |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The doubled expression ('in your cry, cry') is a Semitic intensification idiom. 'Judgment' is the more precise term — the Ge'ez din refers to legal verdict/judgment, not merely justice in the abstract.

---

## 104:5 — 'what shall you be obliged to do?'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "What-shall-ye-be-obliged-to-do?" | Literal rhetorical question |
| LOGOS | "What shall you be obliged to do?" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "What are you going to have to do? Nothing." | Supplies the implied answer |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The rhetorical question implies its own answer (nothing), but the Ge'ez leaves it implied. PNEUMA's explicit 'Nothing' is effective but adds a word not in the text.

---

## 104:8 — 'light and darkness, day and night, see all your sins'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "light-and-darkness, day-and-night, see-all-your-sins" | Literal personification |
| LOGOS | "light and darkness, day and night, see all your sins" | Formal; preserves personification |
| PNEUMA | "light and darkness, day and night — they see everything you do" | 'Everything you do' for 'all your sins' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'All your sins' is the precise Ge'ez term. 'Everything you do' (PNEUMA) broadens the scope unnecessarily and loses the specific moral category.

---

## 104:10 — 'write books concerning their words'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "write-books-concerning-their-words" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "write books concerning their words" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "They will write books supporting their version" | 'Supporting their version' interprets 'concerning their words' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Concerning their words' is intentionally ambiguous — it may mean books about their own teachings (propaganda) or books that distort Enoch's words. PNEUMA's 'supporting their version' over-specifies.

---

## 104:11 — Faithful transmission

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "do-not-change-or-minish-ought-from-my-words" | 'Minish' = archaic for 'diminish'; 'ought' = archaic for 'anything' |
| LOGOS | "do not change or diminish anything from my words" | Formal; modern equivalents |
| PNEUMA | "they do not change them or leave anything out" | 'Leave anything out' for 'diminish' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Diminish' preserves the precise Ge'ez verb (reduce/subtract). 'Leave anything out' (PNEUMA) captures one sense but 'diminish' also includes the idea of weakening the meaning.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 6**
